newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
The central bank does not post volumes.

Traders said the rates went up today, with banks and securities institutions having less money to lend because they were required to pay money to the Finance Ministry this week for underwriting seven-year treasury bonds.
The bonds are being issued from November 1 to 20.

"Although the market is weak, with falling inflation putting downward pressure on the rates, some members had less money to offer today," one trader said. "Others did not have enough funds due to falling enterprise deposits near the year-end."
Traders said the rates were likely to move in a narrow range in the short term. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
